title: Constitutional Law II: individual rights
audience: a law student in a U.S. JD program
purpose: Analyze incorporation of the Bill of Rights, procedural and substantive due process including fundamental rights, equal protection (levels of scrutiny and classifications), freedom of speech, and the free exercise and establishment of religion.
primary_reading: Oyez: U.S. Supreme Court cases and oral arguments

weeks.1: Incorporation of the Bill of Rights
weeks.6: Equal protection: suspect and quasi-suspect classes
weeks.7: Free speech: content-based and content-neutral laws
weeks.8: Public forums and time, place and manner rules
weeks.10: Speech by public employees and students

blocks.deliverable: Decide what process is due before a public employee is fired.
Analyze a fundamental-rights claim and its level of review.
Apply the right tier of scrutiny to four classifications.
Week 7 midterm; analyze a permit rule for a rally in a park.
Decide whether three statements are protected speech.
Analyze a free-exercise challenge to a neutral, generally applicable law.
Submit the project; take an unseen 180 minute final in week 14.

project: Constitutional litigation memo: for a supplied city ordinance written for the course, write a 2,000-word memo analyzing it under the First Amendment, due process and equal protection, with the strongest arguments on both sides.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
